meeting.title: Flock Freight weekly sync
meeting.summary: Thin sync. Colin no-showed for the second consecutive week — finance close ended but he hasn't resurfaced; Jess joined alone and couldn't speak to the migration decisions. The first-10 metric definitions Colin was drafting haven't appeared, the archive announcement hasn't gone out, and the top-20 migration is stalled without his dashboard-by-dashboard input. Jess suspects he's been pulled onto an internal carrier-pricing project. Agreed Ines will reach Colin directly and, failing that, ask Dana-level management who now owns the migration decisions.
action_items: Ines to email Colin directly to re-confirm he still owns the migration shortlist and metric definitions
Jess to ask internally who is covering analytics decisions while Colin is on the pricing project
Ines to propose a shortened catch-up call with Colin rather than waiting for next week's sync
Hold the metrics workstream — do not draft definitions on Vector's side without customer ownership
key_decisions: No proxy decisions: dashboard migration choices wait for Colin or a named replacement, not Vector guesses
meeting.notes: Champion risk is now real: Colin unresponsive for 2+ weeks, portal untouched since before close week, and his two critical deliverables (metric definitions, archive announcement) are stalled. Jess is helpful but explicitly not empowered to make content decisions.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Morning Jess. Just us again? I was hoping Colin would resurface now close week is over.

transcript.speaker: Jess Ortega
transcript.text: Just me, sorry. I pinged him an hour ago — nothing. Honestly I've barely seen him in the office channels either.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: OK, let's be straight about impact. The first ten metric definitions were his; not started as far as we can tell. The archive announcement hasn't gone out. And the top-20 migration needs his call on each dashboard. All three are stalled.

transcript.speaker: Jess Ortega
transcript.text: That matches what I see. Between us — I think he got pulled onto the carrier pricing project after close. It's the CEO's pet initiative this quarter, so it eats people.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: That would explain the silence. The thing is, this project's deadline is real too — the Looker contract non-renewal doesn't move just because attention did.

transcript.speaker: Jess Ortega
transcript.text: I know. I wish I could just make the calls, but I genuinely can't — I don't know which dashboards the ops team lives in. That's exactly the knowledge Colin has.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Understood, and we shouldn't guess on your behalf — wrong migrations are worse than late ones. Here's what I propose: Ines emails Colin directly today, warm but explicit about the three stalled items. If there's no response by Thursday, we ask his management who owns these decisions now.

transcript.speaker: Jess Ortega
transcript.text: Do that. And I'll quietly ask around about the pricing project staffing — if he's seconded for the quarter, better we all know now.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: Agreed. Offer him a twenty-minute catch-up instead of the full sync too — lower the cost of re-engaging.

transcript.speaker: Jess Ortega
transcript.text: Good idea. Sorry this one's gone quiet — it started so well.

transcript.speaker: You
transcript.text: They usually come back. But two silent weeks is exactly when to act, not week six. Thanks for holding the fort, Jess.
